Five derived behavioral-kernel realization endpoints; no five printed theorem attribution. One given Markov-kernel family on generated action and strict observation histories; no reduction of every arbitrary protocol, filtration or private-state algorithm to this model. Classical family selection is an existence result, not a numerical sampler. Five derived actual FTL limit hinges, not five printed results. F1/F2 allow arbitrary real observations for algebra; unit-game feasibility is not claimed for those unbounded streams. F3/F4/F5 require one all-time unit observation stream and the same initial-half strict-past meanPredict. F4 is a limit equivalence, not unconditional existence. F5 explicitly requires empiricalMean convergence; its limit m is analysis-only, never an algorithm input. Fixed-comparator limits may be strictly negative. The existing abstract unbounded-affine counterexample does not settle bounded actual FTL; a concrete bounded oscillating-mean obstruction and all-comparator converse remain separately required source reconciliation. Four derived reconciliation results for the actual initial-half strict-past squared-loss FTL, not four printed source results. D1 is an exact iff for one all-time unit stream: literal comparator-wise finite nonpositive ordinary limits are equivalent to one feasible empirical-mean limit. Necessity adds no mean-convergence premise. D2 produces unit support from the explicit fixed binary dyadic recursion. D3 derives exact prefix counts and two diverging subsequences with distinct mean limits2/3 and1/3. D4 uses the SAME stream and learner: upper-epsilon NoRegret and true interval-best regret/T tends0 coexist with NO finite ordinary limit at fixed comparator0 and failure of literal LimitNoRegret. Signed regret can be negative; no contradiction to the source logarithmic upper bound. No future/horizon-selected observation or mean oracle, stochastic/minimax/all-algorithm impossibility claim. Pinned source ordinary-lim display, existing upper NoRegret and separately proposed source correction remain separate. currentMainValue: Full Chapter 1 source obligations remain separate from this core integration.

The five legacy core modules and their twelve existing proofs are a bounded audit. The original sixteen Chapter 1 source objects remain distinct from an unknown mandatory proof-leaf total; this audit does not complete the chapter, later chapters or required appendix obligations.

These three derived results cover an explicitly specified AE causal information model. The chosen policy is a classical, law-relative version of a given process; equality with the original process is asserted almost everywhere, so values on exceptional null samples may differ. The chosen policy is bounded on every seed/history input and is not an executable learner constructor. General completed-information augmentation and universal causal stochastic-kernel realization remain open. The original sixteen Chapter 1 source objects and unknown required proof total are retained. Remaining Chapter 1 and Chapter 2 obligations, unenumerated Chapters 3–16, and required appendices are separate obligations; these results do not establish chapter or book completion.

One general real-valued measurable-version theorem and three derived causal applications are covered. These are not four printed Orabona theorems. Versions and policies are classical and law-relative; original predictions may differ on exceptional null samples and need not be pointwise causal or everywhere unit-valued. General causal stochastic-kernel realization and other source-required information constructions remain open. The original sixteen Chapter 1 source objects and unknown required proof total are retained. Remaining Chapter 1 and Chapter 2 obligations, unenumerated Chapters 3–16 and required appendices remain separate; no chapter or book completion is established.

Five derived behavioral-kernel realization results are covered, not five printed Orabona theorems. The given kernel family acts on generated unit-action histories and strict real-observation histories. No reduction of arbitrary protocols, filtrations or private-state algorithms to this model is proved. The whole observation stream is independent of the private uniform tape by product construction; action-dependent adaptive environments are outside this model. Conditional-law equality holds almost everywhere under the actual history marginal, while sampler representation holds at every history. Classical sampler selection is an existence result. No regret rate, convergence, pathwise or high-probability guarantee follows. The original sixteen Chapter 1 source objects and unknown required proof total are retained. Other Chapter 1 and Chapter 2 obligations, unenumerated Chapters 3–16 and required appendices remain separate; no chapter or book completion is established.

Five derived results concern the actual initial-half, strict-past squared-loss FTL predictor. The first two are algebraic results for arbitrary real observation streams; they do not assert unit-game feasibility for those streams. The three limit results require one infinite stream with every observation in [0,1]. The fixed-comparator criterion is an equivalence of limits, not an assertion that either limit exists. The final result explicitly assumes empirical-mean convergence; its limit is an analysis parameter and never a learner input. The separate derived dyadic-stream obstruction and all-comparator converse establish these two bounded derived results; broader source reconciliation remains separate. No probabilistic guarantee or nonnegative-regret assertion for arbitrary algorithms is proved. The original sixteen Chapter 1 source objects and unknown required proof total are retained. Other Chapter 1 and Chapter 2 obligations, unenumerated Chapters 3–16 and required appendices remain separate; no chapter or book completion is established.

Four derived results concern the same initial-half, strict-past squared-loss FTL predictor. For any all-time unit-valued stream, finite nonpositive normalized regret limits at every fixed unit comparator are equivalent to convergence of its empirical means. A fixed deterministic dyadic stream lies in [0,1] and has two distinct empirical-mean subsequential limits. For this stream, upper-epsilon no-regret and normalized interval-best regret tending to zero coexist with no finite ordinary limit at fixed comparator zero. This is an obstruction for this specific process, not an impossibility result for all algorithms. Source text and any proposed source correction remain separate; no repair approval is inferred. The original sixteen Chapter 1 source objects and unknown required proof total are retained. Remaining Chapter 1 and Chapter 2 obligations, unenumerated Chapters 3–16 and required appendices remain separate; no chapter or book completion is established.
proposedValue: The source ordinary-limit display is preserved. A bounded actual-FTL counterexample refutes the universal ordinary-limit inference; the separately proved upper property is a derived interpretation, not an approved source rewrite.

Exercises 1.1 and 1.2 remain separate and are not claimed solved. Historical discussion is classified separately. The mandatory proof-leaf total is unknown; no whole-chapter or book completion follows from the 17 claim objects, 54 public contracts or 27 canaries.

The IID results retain a complete independent private-randomness and measurable strict-history model, with explicit AE, completed-information and behavioral-kernel variants. Broader unspecified protocols, side information and action-dependent environments are outside the stated model. Sharp lower-bound constants and an unrestricted minimax equivalence are not proved.

Chapter 2, later chapters and required appendices retain their own obligations. Earlier source cards describe the scope of their individual packages; the current chapter overview reconciles those historical boundaries.

Five derived behavioral-kernel realization endpoints; no five printed theorem attribution. One given Markov-kernel family on generated action and strict observation histories; no reduction of every arbitrary protocol, filtration or private-state algorithm to this model. The entire observation stream is exogenous and independent of the uniform tape: arbitrary temporal dependence is allowed for realization, action-dependent adaptive environments are not covered. Conditional kernel equality is AE under the actual history marginal; every-history sampler representation is a separate conclusion. The IID expected-fixed benchmark takes the infimum of expected fixed unit losses outside expectation; no hindsight min/expectation swap, rate, convergence, pathwise or high-probability bound. Classical family selection is an existence result, not a numerical sampler. Five derived actual FTL limit hinges, not five printed results. F1/F2 allow arbitrary real observations for algebra; unit-game feasibility is not claimed for those unbounded streams. F3/F4/F5 require one all-time unit observation stream and the same initial-half strict-past meanPredict. F4 is a limit equivalence, not unconditional existence. F5 explicitly requires empiricalMean convergence; its limit m is analysis-only, never an algorithm input. Fixed-comparator limits may be strictly negative. The existing abstract unbounded-affine counterexample does not settle bounded actual FTL; a concrete bounded oscillating-mean obstruction and all-comparator converse remain separately required source reconciliation. Five bodies and twelve nondegenerate binary canaries compiled locally; semantic and complete acceptance evidence lives in runs/online-ftl-limit-20261009 and is recorded separately. Original sixteen Chapter1 source objects/null unknown proof total, other C1/C2, unenumerated C3-16 and necessary appendices remain required. Whole Goal ACTIVE; no chapter closure. No probabilistic/rate/high-probability or arbitrary-algorithm nonnegative-regret claim.

Four derived reconciliation results for the actual initial-half strict-past squared-loss FTL, not four printed source results. D1 is an exact iff for one all-time unit stream: literal comparator-wise finite nonpositive ordinary limits are equivalent to one feasible empirical-mean limit. Necessity adds no mean-convergence premise. D2 produces unit support from the explicit fixed binary dyadic recursion. D3 derives exact prefix counts and two diverging subsequences with distinct mean limits2/3 and1/3. D4 uses the SAME stream and learner: upper-epsilon NoRegret and true interval-best regret/T tends0 coexist with NO finite ordinary limit at fixed comparator0 and failure of literal LimitNoRegret. Signed regret can be negative; no contradiction to the source logarithmic upper bound. No future/horizon-selected observation or mean oracle, stochastic/minimax/all-algorithm impossibility claim. Pinned source ordinary-lim display, existing upper NoRegret and separately proposed source correction remain separate. Four bodies and eleven nondegenerate public canaries compiled locally; separate evidence in runs/online-ftl-obstruction-20261009. Only these four derived obligations may close after all gates. Original sixteen Chapter1 source objects/null unknown proof total, full Chapter1 reconciliation, other C1/C2, unenumerated C3-16 and necessary appendices remain REQUIRED. Whole Goal ACTIVE. proposedValue.scope: Accepted-main pre-integration reader state retained exactly; superseded gap labels are historical, not current unresolved claims.
proposedValue.summary: Be-the-Leader and past-mean bounds, a recursive predictor state, comparator domains, finite IID information identities, and a derived logarithmic lower bound for randomized causal guessing in the shared library. Derived no-regret bridges distinguish upper control from ordinary convergence. The attained square-loss minimum connects the explicit best-fixed benchmark to the existing past-mean guarantees.
proposedValue.completion_definition: Bounded integration of the Chapter1 core, arbitrary-initial predictor/recursive state and quantitative derived lower support. Chapter1 and the whole book remain incomplete; the mandatory proof-leaf total remains unknown. The no-regret reconciliation preserves ordinary-limit existence as a separate requirement. The pathwise minimum representation is separate from the expected fixed-loss and causal IID benchmark obligations.
completion_blockers: Full Chapter 1 source obligations remain separate from this core integration.

The five legacy core modules and their twelve existing proofs are a bounded audit. The original sixteen Chapter 1 source objects remain distinct from an unknown mandatory proof-leaf total; this audit does not complete the chapter, later chapters or required appendix obligations.

These three derived results cover an explicitly specified AE causal information model. The chosen policy is a classical, law-relative version of a given process; equality with the original process is asserted almost everywhere, so values on exceptional null samples may differ. The chosen policy is bounded on every seed/history input and is not an executable learner constructor. General completed-information augmentation and universal causal stochastic-kernel realization remain open. The original sixteen Chapter 1 source objects and unknown required proof total are retained. Remaining Chapter 1 and Chapter 2 obligations, unenumerated Chapters 3–16, and required appendices are separate obligations; these results do not establish chapter or book completion.

One general real-valued measurable-version theorem and three derived causal applications are covered. These are not four printed Orabona theorems. Versions and policies are classical and law-relative; original predictions may differ on exceptional null samples and need not be pointwise causal or everywhere unit-valued. General causal stochastic-kernel realization and other source-required information constructions remain open. The original sixteen Chapter 1 source objects and unknown required proof total are retained. Remaining Chapter 1 and Chapter 2 obligations, unenumerated Chapters 3–16 and required appendices remain separate; no chapter or book completion is established.

Five derived behavioral-kernel realization results are covered, not five printed Orabona theorems. The given kernel family acts on generated unit-action histories and strict real-observation histories. No reduction of arbitrary protocols, filtrations or private-state algorithms to this model is proved. The whole observation stream is independent of the private uniform tape by product construction; action-dependent adaptive environments are outside this model. Conditional-law equality holds almost everywhere under the actual history marginal, while sampler representation holds at every history. Classical sampler selection is an existence result. No regret rate, convergence, pathwise or high-probability guarantee follows. The original sixteen Chapter 1 source objects and unknown required proof total are retained. Other Chapter 1 and Chapter 2 obligations, unenumerated Chapters 3–16 and required appendices remain separate; no chapter or book completion is established.

Five derived results concern the actual initial-half, strict-past squared-loss FTL predictor. The first two are algebraic results for arbitrary real observation streams; they do not assert unit-game feasibility for those streams. The three limit results require one infinite stream with every observation in [0,1]. The fixed-comparator criterion is an equivalence of limits, not an assertion that either limit exists. The final result explicitly assumes empirical-mean convergence; its limit is an analysis parameter and never a learner input. The separate derived dyadic-stream obstruction and all-comparator converse establish these two bounded derived results; broader source reconciliation remains separate. No probabilistic guarantee or nonnegative-regret assertion for arbitrary algorithms is proved. The original sixteen Chapter 1 source objects and unknown required proof total are retained. Other Chapter 1 and Chapter 2 obligations, unenumerated Chapters 3–16 and required appendices remain separate; no chapter or book completion is established.

Four derived results concern the same initial-half, strict-past squared-loss FTL predictor. For any all-time unit-valued stream, finite nonpositive normalized regret limits at every fixed unit comparator are equivalent to convergence of its empirical means. A fixed deterministic dyadic stream lies in [0,1] and has two distinct empirical-mean subsequential limits. For this stream, upper-epsilon no-regret and normalized interval-best regret tending to zero coexist with no finite ordinary limit at fixed comparator zero. This is an obstruction for this specific process, not an impossibility result for all algorithms. Source text and any proposed source correction remain separate; no repair approval is inferred. The original sixteen Chapter 1 source objects and unknown required proof total are retained. Remaining Chapter 1 and Chapter 2 obligations, unenumerated Chapters 3–16 and required appendices remain separate; no chapter or book completion is established.
open_gaps: The library proves a finite-horizon lower bound for an explicitly measurable, globally interval-valued seed/history policy class. The source supplies neither this construction nor these constants; sharpness and an unrestricted formal minimax equivalence are not claimed.

The printed ordinary-limit display and eventual upper interpretation are separately reconciled. Equivalence requires actual finite convergence per comparator; no unconditional deterministic comparator-wise ordinary-limit producer for meanPredict or bounded-loss oscillation example is established.
The arbitrary-initial predictor/recursive state does not supply general-initial upper-regret guarantees. General stochastic strategy-class coverage and later module audits remain separate.
Exercises1.1 and1.2 and historical references are classified separately. The mandatory proof-leaf total is unknown; Chapter1 and the whole book remain incomplete.

Finite expected-fixed excess covers deterministic strict-history policies and the explicit whole-process-independent private-tape/subordinate raw-information model. The explicit jointly measurable history-policy class has a stochastic success criterion, and the actual half-initialized mean learner has an IID zero normalized expected-excess limit. General randomized-kernel representation, arbitrary side information, completed or AE information models remain separate; no expectation/minimum interchange is asserted.

Legacy pointwise target support and globally bounded history policies remain stricter APIs. Later almost-sure support, legal-history and private-seed results are separate. Universal stochastic-kernel representation, completed information and almost-everywhere factorization remain open.

originalBaseValue.label: Actual FTL regret and ordinary-limit semantics
originalBaseValue.plain: Let Phi_T be the squared loss of the horizon empirical mean. The actual old leader minimizes the prefix of lengthT. Therefore Phi_(T+1) is at most Phi_T plus the actual next loss. Induct from the empty prefix to obtain Phi_T <= the actual FTL cumulative loss, without a supplied regret premise. Use the proved empirical-mean decomposition for positiveT, and empty sums forT0. Subtract that comparator loss from the same actual cumulative FTL loss. The minus T times squared-distance term is retained exactly. Identify the feasible interval minimum with the produced empirical mean. The actual FTL gap is nonnegative by the first endpoint and at most4+4logT by the source theorem. Divide by positiveT and squeeze between zero and a bound tending to zero. For positiveT, divide the exact comparator identity byT: normalized fixed regret equals normalized best regret minus squared distance from the empirical mean. The best term tends to zero. Subtract limits in both directions to obtain the ordinary-limit equivalence. Assume the empirical mean converges to m explicitly. Continuity gives squared-distance convergence to (u-m)^2 for every fixed realu. The exact equivalence gives fixed regret limit -(u-m)^2. This is nonpositive, so restricting comparators to[0,1] supplies the literal ordinary-limit predicate.

originalHeadValue.math: \begin{aligned}A_T&=\mathbb E[\sum_{t<T}(P_t-Y_t)^2],\quad v=\operatorname{Var}(Y_0),\\\mathcal E_T&=A_T-\min_{u\in[0,1]}\mathbb E[\sum_{t<T}(u-Y_t)^2]=A_T-Tv,\\\mathcal E_T=o(T)&\iff A_T/T-v\longrightarrow0\iff\frac1T\sum_{t<T}\mathbb E[(P_t-\mathbb E Y_0)^2]\longrightarrow0,\\x_0&=\tfrac12,\quad x_t=\frac1t\sum_{i<t}Y_i\ (t>0),\\R_T(x,y)&=\sum_{t<T}(x_t-y_t)^2-\min_{u\in[0,1]}\sum_{t<T}(u-y_t)^2\\&\le4+4\ln T\quad(T\ge1,\ y_i\in[0,1]),\\0\le\mathcal E_T(x)&\le4+4\ln T\ (T\ge1,\ \text{IID}),\quad\mathcal E_T(x)/T\longrightarrow0.\end{aligned}
originalHeadValue.plain: For positive T, (A_T-Tv)/T=A_T/T-v. The standard little-o quotient criterion therefore gives sublinear centered excess iff the average excess tends to zero. The existing causal private-seed producer gives E_T=sum E[(P_t-m)^2]>=0, so this is also equivalent to vanishing Cesaro mean squared deviation. For the actual mean learner, source Theorem1.3 bounds loss minus the empirical hindsight minimum pathwise. That empirical minimum is at most the loss of the fixed population comparator m. Integrate this inequality using derived L2, and use expected fixed loss at m=Tv to obtain E_T<=4+4lnT even without independence. With joint IID the causal lower bound also gives E_T>=0. Sandwich E_T/T between0 and(4+4lnT)/T, whose limit is zero. Apply the same normalization adapter to obtain little-o.

Induct on T: compare the previous prefix with the next feasible leader and then add the current summand. This proves the hindsight Be-the-Leader inequality; supplied minimizers do not define a causal learner. For squared loss, subtract the mean and expand; the centered cross term integrates to zero. For independent random P,Y, covariance vanishes, giving E(P−Y)^2=E(P−EY)^2+Var(Y). The actual x_0=1/2, x_t=t^{-1}Σ_{i<t}Y_i depends only on strict past. Joint target independence and measurable finite sums/division derive its independence from Y_t; measurability and bounds derive L2. Under identical laws, integrate the finite sum, substitute the one-round identity and cancel T·Var(Y_0). Every resulting mean-square term is nonnegative. The population mean is feasible and attains the variance benchmark over ALL real fixed comparators; it is an analysis witness, not a learner input. A measurable scalar policy π_t of the strict finite-history tuple is independent of the current target by disjoint-coordinate independence and composition. Its L2 square identity gives a current-round variance lower bound WITHOUT same-law. Finally divide the scalar residual by T only for T>0. This last equality is not a convergence theorem.

proposedValue.label: A bounded actual-FTL obstruction and exact converse
proposedValue.math: \begin{gathered}\mathrm{LimitNoRegret}(p,y)\Longleftrightarrow\exists m\in[0,1]:\bar y_T\to m,\\ d_t\in[0,1],\qquad\bar d_{4^{n+1}-1}\to\tfrac23,\quad\bar d_{2\cdot4^n-1}\to\tfrac13,\\ \mathrm{UpperNoRegret}(p,d),\quad R_T^{\mathrm{best}}/T\to0,\\ \nexists a\in\mathbb R:R_T(0)/T\to a,\qquad\neg\mathrm{LimitNoRegret}(p,d).\end{gathered}
proposedValue.plain: Use the proposed comparator limits at 0 and 1 and the existing fixed-regret criterion. They give limits for M_T squared and (1-M_T) squared. Their difference plus one, divided by two, equals M_T. Eventual interval membership places the limit in [0,1]. Conversely, empirical-mean convergence yields every comparator limit -(u-m)^2 through the existing FTL producer. Strong induction applies to the strictly smaller parent floor(n/2). The base value is zero; taking one minus a binary value exchanges zero and one. Both outcomes belong to the closed unit interval. The two children at 2k+1 and 2k+2 both equal 1-d_k. Pairing them gives S_(2n+1)=2n-2S_n. Induction yields exact high and low prefix counts. The high mean is exactly 2/3; the low mean is 1/3 minus 1/(3(2*4^n-1)). The two positive natural horizons diverge, so the latter correction tends to zero. Apply the existing actual-FTL upper guarantee and best-regret zero-limit theorem to the proved unit-valued stream. If normalized regret against zero had finite limit a, the existing criterion would force M_T squared to tend to -a. Composition with the two cofinal subsequences forces -a=4/9 and -a=1/9, a contradiction. Since zero is a feasible comparator, LimitNoRegret also fails.
proposedValue.fallback: For every observation stream in [0,1], the actual FTL predictor has a finite nonpositive normalized-regret limit at every fixed comparator in [0,1] exactly when the empirical means converge. The fixed sequence d_0=0 and d_(n+1)=1-d_(floor(n/2)) always lies in [0,1]. Its definition does not depend on a learner or horizon. The same empirical means tend to 2/3 along horizons 4^(n+1)-1 and to 1/3 along horizons 2*4^n-1. On this one bounded stream, the actual FTL predictor has upper-epsilon no-regret and normalized interval-best regret tending to zero, while normalized regret against comparator zero has no finite ordinary limit.

proposedValue.pages: printed 1–7 / PDF 13–19; initialization on printed 3 / PDF 15
proposedValue.plain: For every positive time, both predictors equal the same strict-prefix empirical mean. Split each cumulative prediction loss into time zero and its tail; the tails cancel. Both best-regret expressions subtract the identical comparator infimum, which cancels without a minimum-existence assumption. The remaining term is c=(a-y_0)^2-(1/2-y_0)^2. Reuse the half-initialized quarter-plus-tail bound and add the exact first-round correction c. Expanding 1/4+c gives a^2+(1-2a)y_0. Since a^2<=a, splitting y_0<=1/2 or y_0>=1/2 bounds this expression by 1. The reciprocal tail is unchanged. For each feasible comparator, its regret is at most the interval-best regret. Combine the exact correction with the half-initialized logarithmic bound. The first squared loss is at most 1, so 5+4 log T is an upper bound for positive T. Divide by T and use 1/T and log T/T tending to zero. The actual proof uses this logarithmic route, not the new finite refined theorem. For positive T, divide the exact identity by T. The accepted half-initialized best-regret theorem gives its normalized limit zero, using an actual nonnegative half-FTL loss gap and an upper bound. The fixed correction c divided by T also tends to zero. Adding these two limits and using eventual equality proves the result; an upper bound alone would not suffice.
proposedValue.fallback: For any real initial prediction a, real observation stream y and positive natural horizon T, initialized FTL and half-initialized FTL have exactly the same best-comparator regret except for their first squared-loss difference. With a in [0,1], T>0 and y_t in [0,1] for t<T, initialized FTL has best-comparator regret at most 1 plus four times the reciprocal sum from 2 through T. For one initial a in [0,1] and one all-time unit-valued stream, every fixed comparator u in [0,1] has eventually normalized regret at most each positive epsilon. This is an upper property, without an ordinary-limit claim. For the same legal initialization and all-time unit-valued stream, normalized regret against the best constant comparator in [0,1] tends to zero. No empirical-mean convergence assumption is required.
